intro: Feeder cattle settle in cash on the CME Feeder Cattle Index; live cattle are delivered and converge to the 5-area fed steer price. Positions are shown only for ideas that held up in every period tested (2012-19, 2020-23, 2024-26).

trades.name: Cash convergence (live cattle)
trades.thesis: Live cattle are delivered physically, so the expiring contract converges to the 5-area cash price. Estimate: the latest weekly 5-area price moved along its median path over the same weeks of the last five years. Best tested setting: within 6 weeks, gap above 2.0 $/cwt. Worked in every period tested (2012-19, 2020-23, 2024-26).
trades.entry: Wednesday: if the settlement estimate is above the futures by more than 2.0 $/cwt, buy one lot; below, sell one.
trades.exit: Re-check weekly; close when the gap closes, and in any case before the contract month begins (delivery period).
trades.risk: Weekly cash is thin in some weeks; a single week can move $3-5.

trades.name: 4-week futures trend (feeder cattle)
trades.thesis: Cattle prices move in long cycles; futures inherit part of that persistence. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Wednesday: one lot per contract up to 6 months out in the direction of the signal, when the move exceeds the cost.
trades.exit: Flip or flatten at the weekly check when the signal changes.
trades.risk: Many positions at once; size small.

trades.name: Breakout with trailing stop: live cattle
trades.thesis: Wins less than half the time; stops keep losers small and the occasional long run pays for them. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Daily, on the nearest contract at least 45 days from expiry (2027-02): buy on a settle above the 20-day high (now 234.350); sell on a settle below the 20-day low (now 217.200).
trades.exit: Long: a settle below the 10-day low or the trailing stop (2x the 20-day average daily move below the best close). Short: the mirror. Flat 10 days before expiry.
trades.risk: Average daily move 1.504 $/cwt = $601 per lot; the stop sits about twice that away.
track: Daily settlement vs the 20-day high/low and the stop (this page, nightly)

trades.name: Seasonal pattern (feeder cattle)
trades.thesis: The same contract has moved the same way over the same 4 calendar weeks in at least 70% of the last 5-10 years. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Wednesday: one lot per contract up to 6 months out in the direction of the signal, when the move exceeds the cost.
trades.exit: Flip or flatten at the weekly check when the signal changes.
trades.risk: Many positions at once; size small.

trades.name: Feeder cattle expiry drift
trades.thesis: Feeder cattle settle in cash on the CME Feeder Cattle Index; tests whether being long into expiry pays as it does for live cattle. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Hold one lot long in each feeder contract 4-13 weeks from expiry.
trades.exit: Hold to final cash settlement (the index on the last Thursday of the month).
trades.risk: Feeders swing with corn as well as cattle.

trades.name: Feeders vs the cattle feeding margin
trades.thesis: When finishing cattle is unusually profitable (live cattle 5 months out minus feeders minus corn, against its 3-year range), feedlots bid up feeders; when it is unusually poor, they pull back. Lost money in at least one period tested; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Wednesday: buy the nearest feeder contract when the margin is more than 1.0 standard deviations above its 3-year average; sell when it is that far below.
trades.exit: Close when the margin returns inside the band.
trades.risk: A corn shock moves the margin and the feeders together.
track: Corn, live cattle and feeder futures

trades.name: Live cattle convergence premium
trades.thesis: Live cattle futures have tended to finish above where they traded weeks earlier: feedlots hedge by selling, and buyers are paid to take the other side. But most of that drift arrives in the delivery month itself. Held through the delivery month to expiry, the 0-8-week version has a Sharpe of 1.06 (2012-19 0.75, 2020-23 0.67, 2024-26 2.22); that needs an account that can be assigned delivery of live cattle. Exiting before the delivery month, as a speculative account must, leaves the numbers below. Close to zero in at least one period tested, so no reliable edge; shown for reference, not as a trade.
trades.entry: Hold one lot long in each live cattle contract 0-8 weeks before its contract month begins.
trades.exit: Close on the last Wednesday before the contract month begins (longs can be assigned delivery from the first business day of the month); the test exits there too.
trades.risk: Coincides with a long cattle-cycle bull market; a herd-rebuilding price slump would turn it into steady losses.
track: Cattle on Feed placements and marketings (monthly)
